answer.decision: Choose logical replication with a brief write pause, validation, and traffic switch.
answer.action: Keep the source authoritative while logical replication catches up. During the approved window, pause writes, require replication lag to reach zero, and validate source-to-target row counts and checksums. Switch traffic only if every gate passes with enough time to keep total write unavailability below 10 minutes; otherwise abort the cutover and resume writes on the unchanged source. Keep target writes blocked until validation succeeds and the switch is committed.
reasons: Logical replication is the only listed strategy compatible with the write-unavailability limit: its peak-load staging lag was 42 seconds, while the big-bang option requires a 30-minute freeze.
Keeping the source authoritative through validation protects committed writes and preserves the rehearsed rollback path.
CDC row-count and checksum comparisons provide a concrete correctness gate before the target accepts traffic.
Dual-write would introduce substantial coverage risk across 19 write paths in six modules, including three paths that bypass the main repository layer.
A full export/import is not a viable cutover mechanism because its rehearsal took 96 minutes.
assumptions: Production replication can catch up and validation can complete before a predefined abort deadline within the 10-minute cap.
Schema compatibility, replication configuration, permissions, capacity, observability, and traffic-switch procedures are verified before the window.
Writes can be reliably paused across all application entry points.
The source remains intact and receives no conflicting writes while final replication and validation run.
risks: Production lag or validation may take longer than staging indicated, forcing an aborted cutover.
Row counts and checksums may not detect every application-level semantic inconsistency.
If any writes reach the target before the cutover is committed, rollback could require reverse replication or reconciliation and could exceed the window.
The team's lack of production-cutover experience and absence of overnight vendor support increase operational risk.

citations.claim: The logical-replication staging rehearsal observed 42 seconds of lag at peak synthetic load.
The approved maintenance window permits less than 10 minutes of write unavailability.
CDC monitoring can compare source and target row counts and checksums during cutover.
Rollback to the source was rehearsed in 7 minutes when the source remained authoritative.
Dual-write would have to cover 19 write paths across six modules, including three that bypass the main repository layer.
The full export/import rehearsal took 96 minutes for a production dataset whose largest table is 1.8 TB.
